1.name: Bardic Inspiration
1.notes:
You can supernaturally inspire others through words, music, or dance. This inspiration is represented by your Bardic Inspiration die, which starts as a d6.

Using Bardic Inspiration. As a Bonus Action, you can inspire a creature within 60 feet of yourself who can see or hear you. That creature gains one Bardic Inspiration die. A creature can have only one Bardic Inspiration die at a time.

Within the next hour, when the creature fails a D20 Test, it can roll the Bardic Inspiration die and add the result to the d20, potentially turning failure into success. The die is expended when rolled.

Number of Uses. You can use Bardic Inspiration a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one) and regain all uses when you finish a Long Rest.

At Higher Levels. The Bardic Inspiration die increases to a d8 at level 5, a d10 at level 10, and a d12 at level 15.

1.name: Spellcasting
1.notes:
You have learned to cast spells through your bardic arts.

Cantrips. You know two Bard cantrips of your choice. Dancing Lights and Vicious Mockery are recommended. You learn more cantrips at Bard levels 4 and 10. When you gain a Bard level, you may replace one cantrip you know.

Spell Slots. You use the Bard Features table to determine how many spell slots you have to cast level 1+ spells.

Prepared Spells. You prepare a list of Bard spells equal to the Prepared Spells column of the Bard Features table. Prepared spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

Changing Spells. When you gain a Bard level, you may replace one prepared spell.

Spellcasting Ability. Charisma is your spellcasting ability.

Spellcasting Focus. You may use a Musical Instrument as a Spellcasting Focus.

2.name: Expertise
2.notes: You gain Expertise in two of your skill proficiencies. Performance and Persuasion are recommended. At Bard level 9, you gain Expertise in two additional skills.

2.name: Jack of All Trades
2.notes: You can add half your Proficiency Bonus (round down) to any ability check you make using a skill for which you lack proficiency and that does not otherwise add your Proficiency Bonus.

3.name: Subclass Feature
3.notes: You choose a Bard Subclass and gain its level 3 features. You gain additional subclass features at levels 6 and 14.

4.name: Ability Score Improvement
4.notes: You gain an Ability Score Improvement or a feat of your choice. You gain this feature again at levels 8, 12, and 16.

5.name: Font of Inspiration
5.notes:
You now regain all expended uses of Bardic Inspiration after a Short or Long Rest.

Additionally, you can expend a spell slot (no action required) to regain one use of Bardic Inspiration.

6.name: Subclass Feature
6.notes: You gain a feature from your Bard Subclass.

7.name: Countercharm
7.notes: If you or a creature within 30 feet fails a saving throw against being Charmed or Frightened, you can use a Reaction to make the creature reroll the saving throw with Advantage.

8.name: Ability Score Improvement
8.notes: You gain an Ability Score Improvement or a feat of your choice.

9.name: Expertise
9.notes: You gain Expertise in two additional skill proficiencies of your choice.

10.name: Magical Secrets
10.notes: Whenever your number of prepared spells increases, you may choose new spells from the Bard, Cleric, Druid, or Wizard spell lists. When replacing prepared spells, you may also select spells from these lists.

12.name: Ability Score Improvement
12.notes: You gain an Ability Score Improvement or a feat of your choice.

14.name: Subclass Feature
14.notes: You gain a feature from your Bard Subclass.

16.name: Ability Score Improvement
16.notes: You gain an Ability Score Improvement or a feat of your choice.

18.name: Superior Inspiration
18.notes: When you roll Initiative, if you have fewer than two uses of Bardic Inspiration, you regain uses until you have two.

19.name: Epic Boon
19.notes: You gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat of your choice.

20.name: Words of Creation
20.notes: You always have Power Word Heal and Power Word Kill prepared. When you cast either spell, you may target a second creature within 10 feet of the primary target.
